statement: The Ottoman Empire expanded by absorbing the other Anatolian Turkish beyliks (principalities) — either through conquest or dynastic marriage. Osman I established the beylik in northwestern Anatolia (c. 1300); his successors methodically absorbed neighboring beyliks: Karesi (1345), Germiyan (1390), Hamid (1381), Saruhan (1410). Timur's invasion (1402) temporarily restored some beyliks as Ottoman vassals fled, but Mehmed I reconquered them after the Ottoman civil war (1402–1413). By 1450, the Ottoman state controlled virtually all of Anatolia, with only Karaman holding out until 1468.
